newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs choppy on Sakakibara comments.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs choppy on Sakakibara comments.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures traded choppily on Thursday as comments by key Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara sent players scrambling.
The market rose initially on Sakakibara's comment that Japan was not yet ready to raise interest rates but it then came off when he said he did not rule out a rate rise in the medium term.

Reports quoting a former MOF official saying Sakakibara favoured a yen rate slightly stronger than 120 yen to the dollar pushed the dollar to a high of 115.80 yen, putting pressure on Euroyen and JGB futures, dealers said.
A trader with a Japanese futures house said the falls were limited by players seeking to cover their positions near the low end in view of the recent strong gains in Euroyen futures.
"This recent rally has actually been a squeeze of the short-sellers. No one believed the market would go up so high," he said.
The lead December Euroyen contract was at 99.04 at 1110 GMT after trading in a 99.00-99.07 range against an IMM close at 99.08.
The trader said the contract was likely to be capped at 99.10 and could come back off to test support at 98.95.
"I think Japanese rates should be steady until the middle of next year but I'm still bearish on Euroyen because it looks technically overbought," a trader with a U.S. brokerage said.
She said the December contract faced resistance around its intra-day high of 99.07.
September JGBs ended at 123.61 against their previous 123.87.
Eurodollar futures eased despite the dollar's surge on comments by Federal Reserve Vice Chairman Alice Rivlin, which resurrected fears of a possible U.S. rate hike at the Fed's meeting in July.

Rivlin said in a television interview it was a "close call" on whether the Fed should take steps to slow the U.S. economy. "I'm not sure exactly how I feel right now about what we ought to do in July," she said.
December Eurodollars ended at 93.810 after falling to a low of 93.785 against an IMM close at 93.815 on higher than average volume of 13,105 lots.
